primary.title: The Chemical History of a Candle
primary.author: Michael Faraday
primary.rationale: This is a transcription of a series of lectures given by Faraday in 1848, published posthumously. It offers insights into his understanding of chemistry and physics for a general audience.

primary.title: Experimental Researches in Electricity and Magnetism
primary.author: Michael Faraday
primary.rationale: This is a collection of Faraday's own scientific papers, detailing his groundbreaking experiments and discoveries in electromagnetism. It is a foundational text for understanding his work.

primary.title: A Course of Six Lectures on the Various Forces of Nature
primary.author: Michael Faraday
primary.rationale: Another series of lectures delivered by Faraday, this time focusing on the fundamental forces of nature. It provides accessible explanations of complex scientific concepts.

secondary.title: Faraday, Maxwell, and the Electromagnetic Field: How Two Men Changed the World
secondary.author: Nancy Forbes
secondary.rationale: This book provides a scholarly examination of Faraday's contributions to electromagnetism and his relationship with James Clerk Maxwell, placing his work in historical context.

secondary.title: Michael Faraday: A Biography
secondary.author: L. Pearce Williams
secondary.rationale: While slightly before the 1976 cutoff, this is considered a seminal and highly respected biography of Faraday, offering deep insights into his life and scientific career. It is frequently cited in later scholarship.

secondary.title: The Age of Wonder: How the Romantic Generation Discovered the Beauty of the Heavens
secondary.author: Richard Holmes
secondary.rationale: This book places Faraday within the broader context of the Romantic era's scientific and intellectual landscape, offering a rich historical perspective on his work and influences.

suggestions.notes: The primary sources are collections of Faraday's own writings and lectures, offering direct insight into his scientific thought and communication style. The secondary sources are scholarly works that analyze his life and scientific impact, with a focus on more recent scholarship.
